articles.title: KEI Industries shares surge 7% after Q1FY27 profit jumps 40%, revenue rises 23%
articles.content: Shares of KEI Industries rallied nearly 7% to Rs 5,363.20 on Tuesday following a 40% year-on-year jump in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 274 crore. Revenue from operations rose 23% to Rs 3,185 crore, backed by strong domestic wires and cables demand.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan's Nikkei slips as intervention fears weigh; Toyota earnings in focus
articles.content: Japan’s Nikkei edged 0.11% lower, while the Topix fell 0.26%, as investors remained cautious over possible further yen-buying intervention by authorities and awaited Toyota’s quarterly earnings. articles.title: US Stock Market: Treasury sees higher Q3 borrowing needs as cash flow outlook weakens
articles.content: The US Treasury anticipates borrowing $739 billion in the third quarter. This borrowing estimate reflects lower cash flows and a stronger opening balance. For the fourth quarter, the department projects borrowing of $628 billion. The Treasury borrowed $190 billion in the second quarter, ending June with $919 billion. Investors await debt issuance plans amid market volatility and inflation concerns.

articles.title: Rupee opens on flat note, rises 3 paise to 95.34 against US dollar in early trade
articles.content: The rupee opened flat and gained three paise against the US dollar in early trade. Dollar demand from importers was negated by a weaker dollar index and improved risk sentiment. Lower oil prices and a softer US dollar also supported the rupee's movement. Market participants are now awaiting the upcoming RBI MPC decision and key US economic data. Foreign portfolio inflows into Indian equities provided additional support for the rupee.

articles.title: Global Market: South Korea's July inflation cools below expectations as oil prices ease; rate hike bets remain
articles.content: South Korea's consumer inflation eased to a three-month low in July, falling below market expectations. Lower oil prices significantly contributed to this easing, which was a welcome development. However, policymakers remain cautious about lingering inflationary pressures due to global uncertainties. Core inflation, excluding volatile items, saw a slight increase, indicating underlying price pressures. The Bank of Korea continues to monitor price developments closely for future policy decisions.

articles.title: Nazara Tech Q1 Results: Co posts Rs 82.5 crore loss; Nitish Mittersain steps down as CEO
articles.content: Nazara Technologies reported a net loss of Rs 82.47 crore for the first quarter. Revenue from operations declined 14 percent to Rs 428.77 crore in Q1 FY27. Nitish Mittersain will resign as CEO on September 1, 2026. Raymond Albaladejo Stauffer will succeed Mittersain as the new Chief Executive Officer. The company also revised acquisition terms for Bluetile Games and Bestplay Systems.

articles.title: FIIs build a new Banking XI without the usual heavyweights. Will the big banks return?
articles.content: Foreign investors reduced stakes in large banks during the June quarter. They simultaneously increased holdings in several mid-sized and smaller private lenders. This shift reflects a preference for banks with specific growth triggers and fundamentals. Large banks still offer strong franchises and reasonable valuations for investors. The rotation depends on future earnings and valuation evolution.
